findings.claim: The ported fence-surface tier law failed open through four doors: the corpus walker resolved roots relative to process.cwd, believed the working tree (rm the target file, or name a future file, and the scope was accepted), its catch-branch disarmed it for unreadable directories behind a false justification comment, and no transport re-judged the tier law — the commit-msg gate and push fence judged only scope membership, so a runtime-code task could rewrite gate configs with every gate green (lanes 1f1, 2f1, 4f1, 5f1, 6f4-f6, 7f1, 8f1).
findings.proof: Live end-to-end on the committed tree: from /tmp or tools/, scope --add docs/gates/*.json on a runtime-code task was ACCEPTED; after rm docs/gates/guard-reach.json the exact-path scope was ACCEPTED; the defanging commit then passed the commit-msg gate and the push fence, both of which re-judge containment only.

findings.claim: The guard-reach busy-tree fix was machine-pinned only by a token grep: reverting the baselineEnv call while keeping the unused emptyIndexEnv symbol kept the pin, the self-test, and the whole battery green; and emptyIndexEnv ran outside the try whose job is classifying guard-reach's own failures, dying with a raw stack outside a git repo (lane 7f2).

findings.claim: The freshness mode trusted the client's clone state three ways: git rename detection hid renamed vendored sources (FRESH-FOR-WAVE through a rename, live-proven), a stale clone certified FRESH with no caveat, and a missing --freshness value fell through to host mode's green verdict (lanes 4f2, 4f3, 1f2, 7f4, 7f6).

findings.claim: path-obligations' default mode was structurally blind to untracked files — git diff --name-only HEAD never lists them — so a brand-new fence-surface file printed 'no changed paths ... nothing armed', the exact false silence the tool's header forbids; and the nothing-staged fallthrough mislabeled plain git as jj (lanes 6f1, 5f6, 7f5).

findings.claim: The freshness command pin does not discriminate at the COMMIT level: the recorded RED existed only against a mid-development tree carrying failing seed cases, and a wholesale revert of the freshness half lands on a parent whose own suite is green with every pin green — nothing pins the feature against removal (lane 7f3).
findings.dedupKey: the freshness command pin does not discriminate at the commit level: the recorded red existed only against a mid-development tree carrying failing seed cases, and a wholesale revert of the freshness half lands on a parent whose own suite is green with every pin green — nothing pins the feature against removal (lane 7f3).
findings.justification: A command pin's RED is recorded against pre-fix source by law — it discriminates the FIX, not the feature's lifetime. Wholesale-revert detection is git history's job: the revert commit itself needs a task footer under the fence's citation law, and a reverted feature's future re-request re-pins. Demanding commit-level discrimination from the pin law would require either an always-failing sentinel (vacuous) or a grep of every tool name in every battery (unbounded); the recorded RED-at-fix-time is the strongest collectable form the expect law allows.
